The intrinsic single-crystal κ is 3–4× above the hot-pressed samples. Antisite mass disorder (VCA) closes part of the gap; the rest needs a nanoscale effective mean free path (L_eff ≈ 10–50 nm).

2Calculation setup and convergence

How the force constants were obtained, how far κ is converged in the FC3 cutoff and the q-mesh, and which solver each quoted number comes from. Convergence criterion: a parameter counts as converged when its last refinement step changes κ by less than 10 % (✓ in the tables), the accuracy target of this project. Data: plot_data/convergence_fc3_cutoff.csv, convergence_qmesh.csv, solver_terms.csv.

2.1 Force constants: where FC2 and FC3 come from

check of FC2interlayer TA velocity 1348 m/s vs 1338 m/s from the DFT elastic constants (+0.75 %)interlayer TA 1387 m/s, C₄₄ 9.5–10.3 GPa
κ codephono3py (3.24.0 and 4.4.0; same population term in both)
  • For MnIn₂Se₄, FC2 and FC3 come from two different supercells of the same crystal. Both use the identical relaxed cell (same lattice vectors and atomic positions) and the identical DFT input; the INCAR files differ only in the MAGMOM count, and the k-point density is the same (2×2×1 on 4×4×2 and 2×2×2 on 4×4×1 sample the same k-spacing). Only the size of the supercell along c differs.
  • Why two supercells. In the 4×4×1 cell (one unit cell, 13.2 Å along c) each atom meets its own periodic image across the van der Waals gap, which made the interlayer FC2 far too soft: interlayer TA 323 m/s instead of 1338 m/s. The 4×4×2 FC2 fixes this (1348 m/s). Repeating the anharmonic dataset in 4×4×2 would cost about two days of DFT and does not raise the usable FC3 cutoff, so FC3 stays on 4×4×1.
  • How they are combined. phono3py takes FC2 and FC3 on different supercells (phonon_supercell_matrix = 4×4×2 for FC2, supercell_matrix = 4×4×1 for FC3). ShengBTE cannot, so all MnIn₂Se₄ κ values are from phono3py.
  • Mn₂In₂Se₅ needed no second cell: its 4×4×1 FC2 already gives the correct interlayer TA velocity.

300 K, RTA, isotropic N³ meshes (MnIn₂Se₄ isotopes on; Mn₂In₂Se₅ isotopes off, which changes κ by −1.2 % in-plane and −0.4 % κ_zz). In-plane κ is converged (steps below 3 % from 14³ on). The total κ_zz keeps falling by 12–15 % per step: that is a numerical artifact, because the single q-point next to Γ on the Γ–Z line carries 15–50 % of κ_zz on these meshes and its weight shrinks as N⁻³. Leaving that point out gives the converged term, which changes by less than 1 % per step from 14³ (MnIn₂Se₄) and 24³ (Mn₂In₂Se₅). Chosen: κ_zz = converged term, plateau over 14³–30³ (MnIn₂Se₄, 0.648 ± 0.003) and 24³–32³ (Mn₂In₂Se₅, 0.977 ± 0.008 with isotopes); in-plane MnIn₂Se₄ from LBTE at 14³ with the +1.3 % mesh correction measured on the RTA series, Mn₂In₂Se₅ from RTA at 32³. The κ(T) curves use 14³ and 16³, and the VCA comparison uses 20³ for both (within 3 % of the converged values).

2.4 Solvers: RTA, iterative (LBTE) and Wigner

  • RTA (relaxation-time approximation) gives each phonon its own lifetime and treats every scattering event as resistive. It is cheap and gives the mode-resolved data used for the curves, the mesh and cutoff scans and the disorder models.
  • LBTE (phono3py's direct solution of the linearised Boltzmann equation, equivalent to the converged iterative solution of ShengBTE) solves the full collision matrix, so momentum-conserving Normal processes do not destroy the heat current. In-plane it is higher than RTA by 24 % for MnIn₂Se₄ (14³: 4.5219 vs 3.6474) and 5.9 % for Mn₂In₂Se₅ (10³: 2.9879 vs 2.8220). For κ_zz, LBTE and RTA agree to 4·10⁻⁵. The quoted in-plane values are therefore LBTE-based; κ_zz uses RTA.
  • Wigner (Simoncelli, Marzari, Mauri, Nat. Phys. 15, 809 (2019)) splits κ into the usual population (particle-like) term and a coherence (wave-like) term between modes whose frequencies lie closer than their linewidths. It matters in low-κ, many-branch crystals like these. The coherence term was computed in the RTA (Wigner-RTA) and is added to the population value. Its size at 300 K: MnIn₂Se₄ in-plane 0.091, κ_zz 0.066; Mn₂In₂Se₅ in-plane 0.147, κ_zz 0.112 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, i.e. +2–5 % in-plane and +10–12 % κ_zz.
  • Version rule for the coherence term. phono3py 4.4.0 with SMM19 gives a coherence term 12–17× too large for MnIn₂Se₄, because unregularised soft modes near Γ make it diverge; 3.24.0 and the 4.x IBDB19 option agree with each other. MnIn₂Se₄ therefore uses the 3.24.0 value. The Mn₂In₂Se₅ 4.4.0 value passes the same soft-mode test (−0.3 % in κ_zz when modes below 0.3 THz are removed) and is used.

5Calculation vs hot-pressed experiment

One panel per material and direction. Dashed: ordered single crystal. Solid: VCA antisite-disordered single crystal. Dotted: L3 fit (§8). Dash-dot (MnIn₂Se₄ only): minimum κ from the measured sound velocities (§7). Filled symbols: 300–623 K (used in the fit). Open symbols: 55–145 K (not fitted).

Ordered and VCA: RTA, 20³ (same mesh for each pair), Perp ↔ in-plane, Para ↔ κ_zz, no grain boundary and no texture, so they are upper references. VCA occupancy: MnIn₂Se₄ i = 0.44 (single-crystal refinement, Range et al., Z. Naturforsch. 46b, 1122 (1991)), Mn₂In₂Se₅ x = 0.13 (taken from the L3 fit; the literature value for this R-3m phase is 0.19(2), see §8). VCA lowers κ strongly but stays well above experiment and cannot produce the low-temperature maximum near 100 K; that needs a nanoscale mean free path.

6Scattering rates at 300 K

Largest FC3 cutoff, 20³ mesh, τ⁻¹ = 2Γ. Baseline: real masses + natural isotopes. VCA: averaged site masses + mass-variance scattering. Top row MnIn₂Se₄ (i = 0.44), bottom row Mn₂In₂Se₅ (x = 0.13).

Left: the 3-phonon rates of the ordered and VCA crystals agree within a few tens of percent, because VCA changes the masses, not the anharmonicity. Right: VCA mass-variance scattering is 2–3 orders of magnitude stronger than natural-isotope scattering, rises as ω² at low frequency and flattens at high frequency. Effect on κ at 300 K: MnIn₂Se₄ in-plane 3.69 → 1.49 (2.48×), κ_zz 0.638 → 0.445 (1.43×); Mn₂In₂Se₅ in-plane 3.00 → 1.63 (1.84×), κ_zz 0.984 → 0.792 (1.24×). The weaker effect in Mn₂In₂Se₅ comes from its smaller x.

  • Lattice and Raman: the relaxed structure is within 0.7 % of the single-crystal XRD values, and the two strong Raman peaks match the calculated A1g modes (all Raman-active modes: Eg 26, A1g 75, Eg 95, Eg 168, A1g 176, A1g 260 cm⁻¹). Both support the force constants.
  • Sound velocity: ultrasonic, hot-pressed pellets, two samples (agree within 2 %). The measured v_L is below the calculated v_L in every direction (c axis 3113 m/s is the lowest), so texture cannot explain it; porosity and defect softening of the pellet are the likely reasons. The pellet density is not known yet (theoretical 5.35 g/cm³), so the two cannot be separated. The propagation direction relative to the pressing axis is also not known.
  • Minimum κ (Cahill, Watson & Pohl, PRB 46, 6131 (1992); diffuson model, Agne et al., Energy Environ. Sci. 11, 609 (2018)), n = 0.0376 Å⁻³: the measured κ_tot (Perp 0.93, Para 0.49 at 303 K) lies between the diffuson value 0.20 and the Cahill value 0.62. The hot-pressed samples are close to the amorphous limit, which agrees independently with the strong extrinsic scattering needed in the L3 fit (L ≈ tens of nm). These limits are isotropic; Para lying below the Cahill value is common for layered materials.

8What the L3 fit is

L3 is the extrinsic model of analysis/extrinsic/. Yes, it is fitted to the experimental values, so its agreement with experiment is by construction and is not a prediction.

Γ_λ = Γ_3ph,λ(T) + Σ g_elem(x)·B_elem,λ + |v_λ| / (4π L) 3-phonon Mn↔In antisite mass disorder grain boundary (Casimir) κ_Para = s·κ_xx + (1−s)·κ_zz κ_Perp = (1−s/2)·κ_xx + (s/2)·κ_zz
  • Inputs that are not fitted: the first-principles 3-phonon rates, phonon velocities and heat capacities (ordered masses), and the mass-disorder basis rates B, computed once per material on a 24³ mesh.
  • Three fitted parameters: x, the fraction of Mn on In sites; L, an effective boundary mean free path; s = ⟨sin²θ⟩, the texture (0 = fully textured, 2/3 = random).
  • Data used: only the 300–623 K points of experiment/kappa_tot_digitized.csv, both directions. The fit minimises the rms of ln(model/experiment) over an (x, L) grid, with s optimised at each point. The 55–145 K points are not used; they only test the model.
  • Result: MnIn₂Se₄ x = 0.45, L = 30.7 nm, s = 0.35, rms 1.2 %; Mn₂In₂Se₅ x = 0.13, L = 15.9 nm, s = 0.25, rms 3.2 %.
  • What it does determine: only s (acceptable 0.33–0.38 and 0.15–0.28). x and L both push κ down and are degenerate: acceptable x spans 0–0.66 and 0.01–0.50. The fitted x is therefore not evidence for any occupancy; the closeness of 0.45 to the single-crystal 0.44 is a coincidence of the fit. XRD (texture), SEM (grain size) and a Rietveld occupancy refinement would break the degeneracy.
  • Fixing x from the literature (analysis/disorder/README.md §5.1): MnIn₂Se₄ x = 0.44 (single-crystal XRD, Range et al., Z. Naturforsch. 46b, 1122 (1991)) gives L = 30.7 nm, rms 1.2 %. Mn₂In₂Se₅ x = 0.19(2) (powder Rietveld of the R-3m phase, Williams et al., J. Mater. Chem. C 12, 1753 (2024), ESI Table S7) gives L = 22.1 nm, rms 3.4 %. With x fixed, only L and s are fitted, and L ≈ 20–30 nm in both materials. (The 0.704/0.296 occupancy of Chernoukhov et al., Molecules 30, 1904 (2025) belongs to a different, quenched polymorph, P3̄m1, and is not used.)
  • Not to be combined with VCA: L3 already contains the antisite scattering through x, so the VCA and L3 curves are alternatives, not additive corrections.
  • κ_e is taken as 0. If the electronic part is not negligible, the fitted extrinsic scattering is too strong.

9Caveats

  • The experimental points are digitised from a figure (±0.005 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at high T, ±0.01 at low T) and are κ_tot with κ_e not subtracted. Replace experiment/kappa_tot_digitized.csv once the raw data are available.
  • Mn₂In₂Se₅: the FC3-cutoff steps do not shrink (in-plane −3.9 % → −4.3 %, κ_zz −11.9 % → −9.9 %), so its values are upper bounds and the κ_zz ordering of the two materials is not robust. The in-plane ordering (MnIn₂Se₄ 37 % higher) is.
  • Between the 145 K and 300 K experimental points the Para values drop much more than Perp (Mn₂In₂Se₅ −32 % vs −6 %), possibly two instruments or two samples; this is why the fit uses the high-temperature range only.
